author: Rahul kp
title: Suspense Account
simple_words: If the trial balance does not tally, the gap is parked in Suspense A/c until the errors are found.

definitions.meaning: A temporary account that holds the trial balance difference until the errors causing it are located and rectified.
An error affecting only one account, like a wrong or omitted posting on one side. It upsets the trial balance.

key_points: If the debit total is short, Suspense A/c is placed on the ==debit== side of the trial balance.
If the credit total is short, Suspense A/c is placed on the ==credit== side.
One-sided errors go through Suspense A/c; !!two-sided errors never touch it!!.
Once all one-sided errors are rectified, the Suspense balance becomes nil.

insight.punchline: Suspense is only a parking slot!
insight.text: Once all one-sided errors are rectified through Suspense A/c, its balance becomes nil.

memory_trick.explanation: Suspense is a plug put on the shorter side so totals match. Debit short: Suspense debit. Credit short: Suspense credit.

steps: Find which trial balance side is short
Open Suspense A/c on that side
List each error: one-sided or two-sided
Pass entry; Suspense for one-sided only
exam_tip: Pass a rectifying entry through Suspense A/c only when the error is one-sided; two-sided errors are fixed between the real accounts.

doubt.question: Why does the trial balance difference need no journal entry?
doubt.answer: The difference is simply shown in Suspense A/c on the shorter side of the trial balance. Journal entries are passed only to rectify errors.

mistakes.wrong: Putting Suspense on the credit side when the debit total is short
mistakes.right: Debit total short means Suspense A/c is shown on the debit side.

mistakes.wrong: Passing a Suspense entry for a two-sided error like wrong head of account
mistakes.right: Two-sided errors are rectified between the two accounts concerned; Suspense is not used.
It is debited or credited depending on which trial balance side is short.

Checker 1: Key point 3 / exam tip / mistake 2 (overgeneralisation): 'two-sided errors never touch it' is too absolute. A Suspense entry is needed whenever the original error caused a trial balance difference, even if two accounts are involved. Example: goods sold to X for ₹1,000 were posted to the credit of Y's account. The correction is X A/c Dr ₹1,000; Y A/c Dr ₹1,000; To Suspense A/c ₹2,000. Suggested wording: 'Errors that did not affect the trial balance (where both debit and credit are complete and equal) are rectified between the accounts concerned, without Suspense A/c. Any error that caused a difference in the trial balance is rectified through Suspense A/c.'

Checker 1: Definition 2 (wording): an error 'affecting only one account' also includes casting errors in subsidiary books and errors in carrying forward balances, not just wrong or omitted postings. Say 'e.g.' so the list is not read as complete.
